title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas. The vehicle had a human safety operator present but did not slow down or stop when it hit the duck. Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously at the time.

This incident shows a failure in object detection or response. A deployed autonomous system did not recognize a live animal in its path as something requiring avoidance. The presence of a human safety operator did not prevent the collision, which suggests either the operator did not perceive the duck in time to intervene, or the system's speed or trajectory made intervention impossible.

It is not established whether the vehicle's failure was in perceiving the duck, in classifying it as an obstacle requiring response, or in executing an appropriate maneuver once a hazard was identified. Avride investigated a separate allegation that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and found no evidence for it.

summary:
# Summary

An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck near Mueller Lake, prompting significant community backlash. A resident reported on social media that the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The incident gained attention partly because neighbors had grown attached to the duck, which nested outside a local Italian restaurant. Local residents collected the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator. Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously at the time of the incident.

Following the duck's death, Avride adjusted its testing operations by restricting certain streets around the lake where the incident occurred. The company investigated claims that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and found no evidence supporting this allegation, stating the vehicle made appropriate stops at all relevant intersections. Avride is now conducting simulation experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar incidents without compromising overall safety performance.
